label: Early-sequence unit: first input in {d,w,k,m,b,r,p,l,o}, and copy steps at absolute t<=5 (short sequences)
explanation: Fires near the very start of the sequence in absolute time. It has two parts. (1) At t=0 it fires weakly (about 0.08 of max) when the first token is one of d,w,k,m,b,r,p,l,o. Weaker activity continues at t=1-2 for those same letters. (2) In the copy phase at absolute steps t<=5, which in practice means L=3 or 4 and recall_idx 1-2 (the input is the fed-back orig(0) or orig(1)), it fires for any token. This part holds most of the mass and all the largest activations: the top examples are the step right after <DEL> in L=3 sequences whose first token is d or w (near max). Activation falls off sharply with absolute t and is nearly zero after t~8, so it is essentially silent in long sequences except at t=0. It never fires on the delimiter step or at recall_idx 0. Missed activations: weaker firings at t=1 and at copy steps t=6-7 when the input is in the same letter set. False positives: mostly t=5 copy steps where the input is not in that letter set. Not explained: why that particular letter subset matters.
